answer.summary: Farhan distinguishes a feature as something built on top of existing infrastructure; an experiment is initially for learning, while infrastructure creates reusable foundations for multiple use cases.

sections.heading: What counts as a feature
sections.content: A feature takes advantage of an existing piece of infrastructure. Farhan’s example is token gating: if it can be built in an hour, that suggests the underlying infrastructure is already in place.

sections.heading: How it differs from experiments and infrastructure
sections.content: An experiment starts as something the team is trying in order to learn; it may later turn into an experiment or infrastructure. By contrast, if building the apparent feature also requires creating the infrastructure it depends on, the work belongs in “infra land.” That infrastructure may take longer, but can enable many use cases, including uses of an API the team did not initially anticipate.
